description: Manual food entry: a frozen Spanish copy.es.ts, a zod schema validating name/calories/protein/fat/carbs, and the ManualFoodForm component (react-hook-form + zodResolver) that reuses FormCard/TextField/Button, submits via useAddFoodLog (FEAT-001), and clears on success. Manual entry only — no AI search / external product DB. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/copy.es.ts: export const COPY = Object.freeze({ form: Object.freeze({ title, subtitle, submit, submitting, success, fields: { name, calories, protein, fat, carbs } (Spanish labels, e.g. 'Nombre del alimento','Calorías (kcal)','Proteína (g)','Grasa (g)','Carbohidratos (g)'), errors: { required, nonNegative, positive, integer } }), dashboard: Object.freeze({ title, remainingCalories, protein, fat, carbs, loading, error, empty (no logs yet), noGoal (friendly CTA when no active macro goal), overBudget }) }). Mirror auth/copy.es.ts freezing convention. All user-facing strings in Spanish.

Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/schemas/foodLog.schema.ts: zod schema. name: z.string().trim().min(1). calories: coerce to number, int (z.coerce.number().int()), >= 0 (calories column is integer CHECK >= 0 — coerce/round to int). protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g: z.coerce.number().min(0) (numeric columns accept decimals, non-negative). Export the schema and the inferred FoodFormValues type. Use copy.es error messages where helpful. No any. Document in a comment why calories is int and macros are decimals.

Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/ManualFoodForm.tsx: props { userId: string }. useForm<FoodFormValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(schema) }). Render inside FormCard; use TextField for each field (type='number', inputMode 'numeric' for calories / 'decimal' for macros) with register + errors. PrimaryButton type='submit' (disabled while mutation isPending). On submit, build AddFoodLogInput { user_id: userId, name, calories, protein_g, fat_g, carbs_g } (quantity/unit defaults handled in the data layer) and call useAddFoodLog(userId).mutate(input, { onSuccess: () => reset() }) so the form CLEARS after a successful save. Show the success copy and an elegant error message (COPY.form error, never the raw error) on mutation isError. No useEffect; no console. Functions < 50 lines; file < 400 lines.

Add tests apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/__tests__/foodLog.schema.test.ts (valid payload passes; empty name fails; negative calories/macros fail; non-integer calories is coerced/rounded or rejected per chosen rule; string numeric inputs coerce correctly). ManualFoodForm.test.tsx INTEGRATION: mock useAddFoodLog to capture mutate; render with a userId; fill the fields via RTL userEvent; submit; assert mutate was called with the validated payload (user_id, name, numeric calories/protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g); simulate onSuccess and assert the inputs are cleared (reset). Also assert a validation error blocks submit (mutate not called) and that the error state renders friendly copy, not a raw error string. Mirror auth form test patterns; self-contained (no @energy).
acceptance_criteria: copy.es.ts is a frozen object with Spanish strings for the form and dashboard; schema validates name non-empty, calories non-negative integer, macros non-negative numbers.
ManualFoodForm reuses FormCard + TextField + Button, validates with zod via zodResolver, submits through useAddFoodLog, and resets the inputs after a successful save.
No useEffect used for data fetching; no console calls; zero any.
Integration test proves mutate is called with the validated payload and the form clears on success, and that invalid input blocks submission.
npx vitest run (food-logs) + npm run typecheck + npm run lint pass.
verification: cd apps/macros-web && (energy materialized) npx vitest run src/features/food-logs && npm run typecheck && npm run lint
findings: Implemented the manual food entry surface under apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/. copy.es.ts: frozen COPY with a `form` section (title/subtitle/submit/submitting/success/error, Spanish field labels, errors) AND a `dashboard` section (title, remainingCalories, protein, fat, carbs, loading, error, empty, noGoal, overBudget) for FEAT-003 to consume. schemas/foodLog.schema.ts: zod object with name=z.string().trim().min(1); calories=z.coerce.number().min(0).transform(Math.round) (documented: calories is a Postgres integer CHECK>=0, so fractional input like '120.6' is ROUNDED to 121 rather than rejected); protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g=z.coerce.number().min(0) (numeric(6,2) columns keep decimals). Exports foodLogSchema, FoodFormValues (z.output), foodLogDefaults (empty strings for controlled inputs). ManualFoodForm.tsx: props {userId}; useForm<FoodFormValues> + zodResolver, mode 'onTouched'; reuses FormCard/TextField/PrimaryButton; builds AddFoodLogInput {user_id,name,calories,protein_g,fat_g,carbs_g} (quantity/unit defaults handled by the data layer) and calls useAddFoodLog(userId).mutate(input,{onSuccess:()=>reset(defaults)}) so the form clears on success; shows success copy on isSuccess and friendly COPY.form.error on isError (never a raw error); submit disabled + 'Guardando...' while isPending; NO useEffect, NO console. Tests: foodLog.schema.test.ts (8) and ManualFoodForm.test.tsx (7, integration via mocked useAddFoodLog capturing mutate) — assert validated numeric payload incl. user_id, reset-on-success clearing all inputs, invalid input (empty name / negative calories) blocks mutate, friendly error vs raw, pending/success states. DEVIATION: used the macros-wizard pattern useForm<FoodFormValues> with defaultValues/reset cast via `as unknown as DefaultValues<FoodFormValues>` because z.coerce/.transform make the schema input (strings) differ from output (numbers) and RHF's resolver generic cannot reconcile both cleanly; this mirrors MacrosWizard.tsx exactly. ENV: energy domain was materialized at APP/src for the full-suite run then removed (git status clean of src/ before commit). Verification: npx vitest run src/features/food-logs = 35/35; full suite 191/191; npm run typecheck clean (zero any); npm run lint clean (no-console); food-logs feature coverage 100% stmts/funcs/lines, 93% branch. New tests contain no @energy import (grep verified).
